No. These twelve owner-selected screenshots cannot establish SOC 2 readiness or support certification or an independent assurance opinion.

The supplied facts establish owner selection, an unknown population and no independently selected evidence. They do not establish what the screenshots contain, whether controls failed, or whether logs or metadata are absent. The assessment period, control frequency, metadata, design and operating effectiveness remain unknown until examined. Owner selection limits representativeness; it does not establish motive or the direction of bias.

Report insufficient evidence to conclude readiness for the assessment scope and period, which still need clarification. Screenshots can support specific observations after inspection, without supporting a population-wide conclusion. A management readiness review is not an independent assurance opinion.

Agree the system boundary, applicable criteria and period, and separate design adequacy, point-in-time implementation and operation over the period. Define each relevant control, owner, frequency and full evidence population; check population completeness against an independent source where available. Examine screenshot provenance and period relevance, then select additional evidence independently and reproducibly using a method justified by control risk and frequency. Do not invent a universal sample count or statistical confidence from these twelve items.

Test the selected items against the criteria and record evidence keys, exceptions, missing evidence, out-of-scope items and unexecuted tests separately. Report proven deficiencies separately from evidence gaps, with supported consequences and proposed remediation and retest. Keep sampling and independence limitations next to the conclusion. The present deliverable is an evidence-readiness gap list and bounded assessment plan, not a certificate.
